agents.verdict: Keep the romance scene on the unspoken emotional request.

options.name: Future Witness Scenes
options.case_for: Best for exact-copy commitment text: conflict, repair, older-couple witness, bad-day cost, and future-us payoff become clear staged scenes.
options.risk: Must not copy the reference film stills or become generic elderly-couple quote art; Aachu/Zuv identity and house style must dominate.

options.name: Hands Stay Reachable
options.case_for: Very strong for conflict-with-commitment because hands, distance, and posture prove the text without heavy explanation.
options.risk: Can become visually repetitive if every slide is only a close-up handhold.

options.name: Older Couple Mirror
options.case_for: Clear reference to the older-couple idea.
options.risk: Rejected as the main system because the older couple can overpower Aachu/Zuv and make the deck less identity-first.

final_visual_plan.copy: We disagree, I still love you.
final_visual_plan.visual: A close evening domestic frame after a small disagreement: Aachu and Zuv are turned slightly away from each other, but their knees, shoulders, and one almost-touching hand still lean toward the same center. The mood preserves the reference's intimate conflict-with-commitment feeling without copying its dark film still.

final_visual_plan.copy: We fight, I still love you.
final_visual_plan.visual: After the fight, Aachu folds into Zuv's shoulder in a warm doorway or sofa corner; his hand is steady at her back, her face softened but still emotional. The hug is the proof that the conflict stayed inside commitment.

A small close-up proof beat of their hands finding each other again on a couch, car seat, or cafe bench; one finger hooks around the other while the rest of the room fades into warm paper. The question opens the emotional turn.

final_visual_plan.copy:
Because every time I see an older couple,
standing side by side,
I think about everything it took to get there.
final_visual_plan.visual: Aachu and Zuv quietly notice an older couple standing side by side in a soft gallery, garden path, or cafe queue. The older couple is small and respectful in the background; Aachu and Zuv are the emotional focus, watching the proof of time.

final_visual_plan.copy:
All the arguments.
All the bad days.
All the times they could’ve walked away,
but didn’t.
final_visual_plan.visual: A staged memory-collage without becoming a collage: one wide warm scene shows traces of hard days around them, such as two untouched cups, a wrinkled blanket, a paused phone, and rain at the window, while Aachu and Zuv remain near each other instead of walking out of frame.

final_visual_plan.copy:
And then I think of us.
Because I know that’s going to be us one day.
final_visual_plan.visual: Aachu and Zuv in a lived kitchen or balcony moment, preparing something small together or standing shoulder to shoulder; a faint future echo of an older version of them appears only as soft background warmth, not as a literal copied elderly couple.

final_visual_plan.copy:
Still together.
Still choosing each other.
Still completely in love.
final_visual_plan.visual: Final airy frame: Aachu and Zuv sit side by side at a small table or overlook, older-couple energy translated into their own present-day bodies. He is calm and close, she is soft and expressive, and both faces are clear, warm, and identity-first.
